To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a model to enable the co-existence and co-operation of applications in the context of a strongly partitioned real-time system.
the proposed model is able to guarantee spatial and temporal isolation for all the applications in the system and also enable them to access shared I/O devices.
the proposed device-sharing model provides a mechanism to share the device among the application in a partitioned environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing a device sharing model that can be used by applications in a strongly partitioned environment.
the following issues: • How to design a device-sharing model that supports temporal partitioning of I/O devices in the presence of a microkernel-based real-time operating system (RTOS).

this work is the first to address the sharing of I/O in a microkernel-based environment for strongly partitioned real-time system.
our approach provides a simple yet effective model for sharing IO devices in strongly partitioned real-time environments.
this paper provides a model for device sharing that can be used to integrate the device sharing model with the micro-kernel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach provides a flexible and efficient solution for sharing I/O devices and resources in strongly partitioned real-time environments.
the model enables a real-time system with a set of co-existing applications to share I/O devices in a safe and efficient way.
the device-sharing model is able to provide the required spatial and temporal isolation for applications and the microkernel is capable of providing the necessary services for device-sharing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the device-sharing mechanism does not need to know the details of applications and the microkernel can be used for the integration.
the model can provide a flexible and efficient way to support device sharing in strongly partitioned systems.
the device-sharing model can be effectively integrated with a microkernel-based real-time system.
